    - heading "Amazon RDS" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Easy to manage relational databases optimized for total cost of ownership.
    - button "Get started with RDS"
    - button "Connect with an RDS specialist"
    - heading "What is Amazon RDS?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) is a fully managed relational database service optimized for total cost of ownership. It automates provisioning, configuration, backups, and patching across nine database engines and two deployment options, serving developers and database administrators who need production databases without provisioning infrastructure or maintaining software.
    - button "Play:"
    - img "Missing alt text value"
    - heading "How much does Amazon RDS cost?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Try Amazon RDS for free
    - paragraph: New AWS customers receive up to $200 in AWS Free Tier credits, which can be applied towards eligible AWS services, including Amazon RDS. The free plan is available for 6 months after account creation.
    - paragraph:
      - link "Learn more about the AWS Free Tier":
        - /url: /free/?p=pdp&c=rds&s=3
    - paragraph: On-demand
    - paragraph: Pay per hour for database instances with no upfront commitment and no long-term contract.
    - paragraph:
      - link "View detailed pricing":
        - /url: /rds/pricing/?p=pdp&c=rds&s=3
      - text: Database savings plan
    - paragraph: Commit to a specific amount of usage, measured in $/hour, over a 1-year term and save in exchange for your commitment.
    - paragraph:
      - link "Learn more about savings plans":
        - /url: /savingsplans/database-pricing/
    - heading "What problems does Amazon RDS solve?" [level=2]
    - paragraph
    - heading "Time-consuming administration" [level=3]
    - img "Abstract tech illustration representing Amazon AI with colorful geometric panels and flowing ribbon shapes in grid structure"
    - text: RDS runs managed relational databases without provisioning infrastructure or maintaining software. Teams remove undifferentiated management tasks such as provisioning, configuring, backing up, and patching, and can create a new database in minutes.
    - heading "Keep business critical workloads online" [level=3]
    - img "Abstract visual of smooth vertical ribbons curving inward and upward, symbolizing business agility through Infor Marketplace on AWS"
    - text: RDS delivers high availability and enterprise reliability out of the box with multi-AZ deployments and automated failover, ensuring business continuity without manual configurations. Your data is synchronously replicated across Availability Zones, so business-critical workloads stay online during instance or AZ disruptions.
    - heading "Choosing between performance and cost" [level=3]
    - img "aws-library_illustration_data_11_1200"
    - text: RDS helps you optimize database performance and costs. You can utilize AWS innovations like custom silicon, the AWS Nitro System, and elastic infrastructure alongside the latest instances, optimized reads and writes, and flexible pricing.
    - heading "Migrations that require re-architecting" [level=3]
    - img "aws-library_illustration_connect_7_1200"
    - text: RDS enables simple lift-and-shift migration from self-managed databases with minimal code changes. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, and Db2. Once in the cloud, your data is next to the agentic AI, ML, and analytics services that need it.
    - heading "How does Amazon RDS work?" [level=2]
    - heading "1. Choose your database engine" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Choose your database engine and deployment option in the console or API. RDS provisions the instance and configures networking and storage automatically.
    - heading "2. Load your data" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Load your data using standard tools and connect your application using standard database drivers. Existing open source and commercial applications work with minimal to no code changes.
    - heading "3. RDS automates database management" [level=3]
    - paragraph: RDS handles backups, patching, and monitoring on your behalf. Multi-AZ deployments synchronously replicate data and manage failover automatically.
    - heading "4. Scale capacity with demand" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Scale compute, storage, or read capacity as demand changes. Features such as optimized reads, optimized writes, and Graviton5-based instances help improve performance.
    - heading "What are the top Amazon RDS use cases?" [level=2]
    - heading "Build web and mobile applications" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Support growing apps with high availability, throughput, storage scalability, flexible pay-per-use pricing.
    - heading "Move to managed databases" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Innovate and build new applications without self-managing databases, which can be time consuming, complex, and expensive.
    - heading "Power agentic AI applications" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Run vector workloads on Aurora and RDS for PostgreSQL for retrieval and semantic search.
